evidence.note: Explicit correctness-first plan; built a reference test and confirmed the baseline PyTorch kernel matches it exactly before touching performance — a clear reference→correct-kernel milestone with a done-check.
Optimization only began after correctness was established; benchmarking treated as a distinct phase, showing intentional ordering of stages.

Whenever a bf16 optimization broke correctness, the agent reverted and kept a fp32 correct path — the correctness gate was maintained as a separate track throughout optimization, catching fast-but-wrong regressions.

The optimization stage itself was reactive trial-and-error (compile modes, custom Triton kernels, casting, contiguous tweaks) with no decomposed per-shape milestones or structured exit criteria, so it doesn't reach the top anchors.

reasoning: The agent clearly separated correctness from performance: it built a reference oracle, verified a correct baseline against it, and only then optimized, consistently reverting speed changes that violated tolerance (matching and slightly exceeding anchor 5 via a maintained correctness gate). It falls short of anchor 8 because the naive kernel was not verified across the full shape/dtype/mask grid as an explicit milestone, and the optimization phase was undecomposed, reactive experimentation rather than checked per-shape sub-milestones.
